title: Day 2 Diagnostic — Introduce yourself without a script
purpose: Kiểm tra khả năng chọn thông tin, đóng gói identity, dùng thought groups/chunks và trao lượt nói — không kiểm tra học thuộc một đoạn giới thiệu.

questions.prompt: You meet another engineer for the first time. Which opening gives useful information and a natural conversation hook?
options: My name is Lương. I am a person. I have many hobbies.
I work. I like technology. Thank you.
I'm based in Vietnam and I work mainly on backend integrations. These days, I'm also building AI projects.
I am backend integration software person from many years.
questions.explanation: A natural introduction selects relevant identity information and gives a specific hook the listener can respond to.

questions.prompt: Which sentence best presents a relatively stable professional domain?
options: I work in software integration.
I'm working in software integration yesterday.
I've work in software integration.
I working software integration.
questions.explanation: Present Simple naturally frames a current role/domain as a relatively stable fact: 'I work in…'.

questions.prompt: What is the best speaking strategy for: “I'm based in Vietnam and I work in software integration”?
options: Give every syllable exactly the same weight.
Pause after every single word.
Speak it as one breath with no grouping.
Use thought groups, for example: 'I'm based in Vietnam / and I work in software integration.'
questions.explanation: Thought groups package meaning into listener-friendly units. The slash represents a light boundary, not a dramatic pause.

questions.prompt: You want to explain what your job actually consists of, not just name the field. Which frame is most useful?
options: My work is title.
Most of my work involves connecting different systems.
I am involving work.
My work contains job.
questions.explanation: 'My work involves + noun/V-ing' is a natural frame for describing the activities a role includes.

questions.prompt: After a 30-second introduction, which move most naturally turns the monologue into a conversation?
options: Continue listing every project you have done.
Repeat your job title more slowly.
Ask 'What about you?' and listen to the answer.
End with 'That's all information.'
questions.explanation: 'What about you?' redistributes the floor and creates reciprocity, a core feature of conversational introductions.

questions.prompt: You realize your first description was too broad: “I work in security systems…” Which Day 1 chunk helps you refine the statement naturally?
options: I mean, mostly software integration.
Fair enough, mostly software integration.
No worries, mostly software integration.
Sounds good, mostly software integration.
questions.explanation: 'I mean' supports self-repair and clarification. This is intentional Day 1 retrieval in a new context.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between “I'm into AI” and “I'm an AI expert”?
options: There is no difference.
'I'm into AI' can express interest without claiming expertise.
'I'm into AI' is always formal business English.
'I'm an AI expert' only means you enjoy AI.
questions.explanation: 'Be into' normally expresses interest/enthusiasm. It does not by itself claim professional expertise.

spokenChallenge.prompt: Record a 60-second introduction for meeting a new international colleague. Include your work/domain, one current focus, one personal interest, one specific hook, and end by giving the other person a turn. Use one Day 1 discourse marker only if it genuinely helps the flow.
